record.narrative: All twelve discovery cells satisfy the minimum cell-size and validity requirements, so the main scientific issues are direction, uncertainty, clinical magnitude, multiplicity, and possible confounding. I interpret the displayed estimates as already direction-signed: a positive signed estimate supports the registered hypothesis direction, whereas a negative signed estimate supports the opposite raw contrast. No comparison is causal; all are single-marker associations in this supplied dataset, potentially influenced by predictor correlation and outcome correlation.  H1, H3, H5, H7, H10, H11, and H12 show small registered-direction estimates with 95% Welch intervals that do not approach the approximate 10% relative-dependency threshold for the claimed direction; several are also close to zero in absolute score units. H2 and H4 similarly do not support their registered directions, although their intervals are wide enough to leave some opposite-direction uncertainty. I reject these as registered-direction claims and close them.  H6 remains potentially relevant: for outcome_007, the signed estimate is positive (registered direction, stronger dependency), with a lower raw-effect bound that could cross a clinically meaningful ~10% threshold, but the interval also includes zero and opposite values. It is unresolved and deferred pending priority follow-up. H8 is the most promising registered-direction claim: outcome_014 has a signed effect of +0.0319 (raw exposed-minus-comparator approximately -0.032, i.e., more negative/stronger dependency), which is large relative to the approximately -0.09 mean of outcome_014, but the interval still crosses zero. It remains unresolved and active rather than accepted.  The only interval excluding zero is H9, but it excludes zero in the opposite direction: feature_006-positive cells have a signed estimate of -0.038 for outcome_010, implying a raw positive contrast of about +0.038 (less negative, weaker dependency). Relative to an estimated comparator mean near -0.255, that is roughly a 15% relative effect, so it is scientifically meaningful but contrary to H9's registered direction. Therefore H9 must be rejected. Because it is also the strongest candidate signal after multiple unadjusted comparisons, I request independent validation of H9 to determine whether this robust-looking opposite association is reproducible or a chance discovery. I also register the logically reversed H13 for feature_006 versus outcome_010 as a follow-up association test.  Overall, no original claim can currently be accepted.
